match.reason: Neither bank point teaches resolving a vector using the scalar product along and perpendicular to another vector; the physics points only cover scalar versus vector basics and splitting forces into horizontal and vertical components at right angles, which is a different idea and depth.

draft.title: Scalar and vector resolutes
card: Scalar resolute
The scalar resolute of a in the direction of b is a·b ÷ |b|. It is a number: the signed length of a along b. It is negative if a points against b.
Vector resolute
The vector resolute of a parallel to b is (a·b ÷ |b|²) b. It is a vector along b. Its length is the size of the scalar resolute.
The part of a perpendicular to b is a − (the vector resolute). Its scalar product with b is 0.
Example: a = 2i + 3j + 6k, b = i + 2j + 2k. Then a·b = 20 and |b| = 3. The scalar resolute is 20/3. The vector resolute is (20/9)(i + 2j + 2k).
draft.remember: Scalar resolute is a length along b. Vector resolute puts that length on the direction of b.

a.q: What is the scalar resolute of a = 3i + 2j + 2k in the direction of b = 2i + j + 2k?
a.why: a·b = 6 + 2 + 4 = 12 and |b| = √(4 + 1 + 4) = 3, so the scalar resolute is 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Dividing by |b|² gives 4/3, which is the mistake of using the vector resolute's divisor.
a.clue: Divide a·b by the length of b, the vector you project onto.

b.q: What is the vector resolute of a = i + 4j + 3k parallel to b = 2i − j + 2k?
b.why: a·b = 2 − 4 + 6 = 4 and |b|² = 9, so the vector resolute is (4/9)(2i − j + 2k). Dividing by |b| instead of |b|² gives the second option. The last option is the perpendicular part, a minus the resolute.
b.clue: Divide by |b|², not |b|, then multiply by b.

problems.detail: The why for (b) mixes up the distractors. Dividing by |b| instead of |b|² gives (8/3)i − (4/3)j + (8/3)k, not (1/9)i + (40/9)j + (19/9)k. The perpendicular part, a minus the resolute, is (1/9)i + (40/9)j + (19/9)k, not (8/3)i − (4/3)j + (8/3)k. The why should name these options by their values, not by position.
The remember line calls the scalar resolute 'a length along b', but the card says it is a signed length that can be negative. Dropping 'signed' may lead students to think it is never negative.

check.summary: The card and both intended answers are correct (a: 4, b: (8/9)i − (4/9)j + (8/9)k). The why for (b) swaps the two distractors it describes, and the remember line drops 'signed' from the scalar resolute.

final.title: Scalar and vector resolutes
card: Scalar resolute
The scalar resolute of \(a\) in the direction of \(b\) is \(\frac{a \cdot b}{|b|}\). It is a number: the signed length of \(a\) along \(b\). It is negative if \(a\) points against \(b\).
Vector resolute
The vector resolute of \(a\) parallel to \(b\) is \(\left(\frac{a \cdot b}{|b|^{2}}\right)b\). It is a vector along \(b\). Its length is the size of the scalar resolute.
The part of \(a\) perpendicular to \(b\) is \(a - (\text{the vector resolute})\). Its scalar product with \(b\) is 0.
Example: \(a = 2i + 3j + 6k\), \(b = i + 2j + 2k\). Then \(a \cdot b = 20\) and \(|b| = 3\). The scalar resolute is \(\frac{20}{3}\). The vector resolute is \(\frac{20}{9}(i + 2j + 2k)\).
final.remember: The scalar resolute is a signed length along \(b\). The vector resolute is that signed length times the unit vector of \(b\).

a.q: What is the scalar resolute of \(a = 3i + 2j + 2k\) in the direction of \(b = 2i + j + 2k\)?
a.why: \(a \cdot b = 6 + 2 + 4 = 12\) and \(|b| = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 4} = 3\), so the scalar resolute is \(12 \div 3 = 4\). Dividing by \(|b|^{2}\) gives \(\frac{4}{3}\), which is the mistake of using the vector resolute's divisor.
a.clue: Divide \(a \cdot b\) by the length of \(b\), the vector you project onto.

b.q: What is the vector resolute of \(a = i + 4j + 3k\) parallel to \(b = 2i - j + 2k\)?
b.why: \(a \cdot b = 2 - 4 + 6 = 4\) and \(|b|^{2} = 9\), so the vector resolute is \(\frac{4}{9}(2i - j + 2k) = \frac{8}{9}i - \frac{4}{9}j + \frac{8}{9}k\). Dividing by \(|b|\) instead of \(|b|^{2}\) gives \(\frac{8}{3}i - \frac{4}{3}j + \frac{8}{3}k\). The answer \(\frac{1}{9}i + \frac{40}{9}j + \frac{19}{9}k\) is the perpendicular part, \(a\) minus the resolute.
b.clue: Divide by \(|b|^{2}\), not \(|b|\), then multiply by \(b\).
